title: Spatial information explained by prediction models under block cross-validation
venue: ISPRS Journal of Photogrammetry and Remote Sensing
abstract: Spatial information in geographic data arising from the dependence between variable values and their locations fundamentally shapes the performance and evaluation of spatial prediction models. Model evaluation primarily relies on global accuracy metrics such as root mean squared error (RMSE), which quantify prediction error but do not assess spatial structure a model explains in observed data. However, there are still challenges in the spatial information as a measurable quantity in prediction modelling and the assessment of spatial learning performance under spatial block cross-validation. This study develops the spatial information explained (SIE) metric to assess the extent to which spatial prediction models explain spatial information during modelling, through quantifying the relative reduction in spatial information from a response variable to its prediction residuals. SIE integrates block cross-validation residual computation that enforces spatial separation between training and evaluation sets, and mutual information-based quantification of spatial information contents, and softmax-weighted multi-scale aggregation. A spatial simulation study validates that SIE is effective in measuring spatial learning performance. The developed SIE metric is implemented in predicting C4 natural grass area percentage across Australia with multi-source environmental data of photosynthetic advantage, temperature, and precipitation variables, and ten machine learning models evaluated under block and random cross-validation. Results show that SIE effectively distinguishes machine learning models in spatial learning performance, and reveals that model rankings under SIE differ from those under RMSE, and prediction accuracy and SIE represent distinct evaluation dimensions. Specifically, KNN, the neural network, and XGBoost achieve the highest multi-scale SIE of approximately 0.50 together with high prediction accuracy, SIE rankings correlate weakly with accuracy rankings across the ten models, and random cross-validation overstates SIE relative to block cross-validation for all ten models, by 2.1% to 17.0% with a mean of 9.9%. The validation power of SIE arises from the information-theoretic property that mutual information captures all forms of spatially statistical dependence between residuals and spatial location, including nonlinear spatial associations that domain-average accuracy metrics cannot detect. SIE measures spatial learning performance that complements conventional accuracy metrics, with broad applicability to spatial prediction tasks in Earth and social sciences, and advanced geospatial artificial intelligence and foundation modelling, where capturing geographic structure is analytically required.

title: Global asymmetric mangrove-edge shifts reveal coastal squeeze under sea-level rise
abstract: Changes at the land–sea interface reveal whether mangrove systems advance seaward, retreat landward, or undergo coastal squeeze as their seaward and landward boundaries converge. Yet global assessments have largely relied on area change, with less focus on these directional processes. This study applies a global coastline-normal transect framework to Global Mangrove Watch data for 1996, 2008, and 2020. By quantifying the seaward and landward edges together with width and centroid position, we distinguish expansion, directional migration, and contraction across multiple spatial scales. Globally, mangroves lost an average width of 77.2 m: the seaward edge retreated landward by 47.5 m, a pattern consistent with marine forcing including relative sea-level rise and coastal erosion, while the landward edge shifted seaward by 53.7 m, compatible with restricted accommodation space. Together, these opposing movements reveal widespread asymmetric contraction. Among regions exhibiting clear directional migration, 65.2% shifted seaward, including advances of up to 2.5 km in Marajó Bay, Brazil, whereas less frequent landward migration reached 5.6 km in the northern Gulf of Mexico. After 2008, the prevalence of landward migration increased, particularly across Asia and Africa. The edge trajectories constrain the set of plausible controls but do not uniquely attribute change to sea-level rise, sediment supply, topography, land use, or restoration. Conservation should therefore protect potential landward migration pathways while accounting for uncertainty in the mechanisms producing individual local trajectories.

title: Multi-task learning for simultaneous surface water and burned area mapping from earth observation data
abstract: Multi-task learning has emerged as a promising approach for combining related tasks into a unified framework with reduced computational costs through shared representations. However, its application to hazard mapping using Earth Observation data remains underexplored. In this study, we provide the first systematic evaluation of multi-task deep learning architectures for simultaneous detection of crisis information (surface water and burned area) using Sentinel-2 and Landsat-8 optical imagerytwo societally critical hazards with strong operational demand for rapid and accurate detection. We evaluate five semantic segmentation architectures: three U-Net variants with different encoders (MobileNetV2, EfficientNet-B4, ResNet50) and two transformer-based SegFormer models (SegFormer-B0, SegFormer-B4). Each architecture was trained in both single-task learning and multi-task learning modes. For reference data, we employed the benchmark S1S2-Water dataset for water body detection and constructed a novel burned area dataset by integrating diverse global datasets with already available in-house annotations. Both reference datasets cover heterogeneous geographic regions and temporal periods. The results show that multi-task learning effectiveness is highly architecture-dependent. Burned area detection achieved F1-scores ranging from 0.624 to 0.701, with three of five architectures showing improvements under multi-task learning. SegFormer-B4 reached the best performance (F1-score: 0.67) with gains of +8.24% over its single-task baseline, while EfficientNet-B4 achieved the highest absolute accuracy (F1-score: 0.701). Conversely, ResNet50 exhibited negative transfer with an F1-score decrease of 8.24%, demonstrating that not all architectures benefit from multi-task learning. Water detection performance remained consistently high across all models (F1-score > 0.97), with SegFormer-B4 achieving an F1-score of 0.98. Importantly, the multi-task framework reduces inference time by 89–91% and parameter count by 17–48% compared to maintaining two separate single-task models, demonstrating its practical value for operational emergency mapping services where rapid hazard assessment is critical.

title: Privacy Leakage on DNNs: A Survey of Model Inversion Attacks and Defenses
HR-INR: Continuous Space-Time Video Super-Resolution via Event Camera
abstract: Abstract Continuous space-time video super-resolution (C-STVSR) aims to simultaneously enhance video resolution and frame rate at an arbitrary scale. Recently, implicit neural representation (INR) has been applied to video restoration, representing videos as implicit fields that can be decoded at an arbitrary scale. However, existing INR-based C-STVSR methods typically rely on only two frames as input, leading to insufficient inter-frame motion information. Consequently, they struggle to capture fast, complex motion and long-term dependencies (spanning more than three frames), hindering their performance in dynamic scenes. In this paper, we propose a novel C-STVSR framework, named HR-INR, which captures both h olistic dependencies and r egional motions based on INR. It is assisted by an event camera – a novel sensor renowned for its high temporal resolution and low latency. To fully utilize the rich temporal information from events, we design a feature extraction consisting of (1) a regional event feature extractor – taking events as inputs via the proposed event temporal pyramid representation to capture the regional nonlinear motion and (2) a holistic event-frame feature extractor for long-term dependence and continuity motion. We then propose a novel INR-based decoder with spatiotemporal embeddings to capture long-term dependencies with a larger temporal perception field. We validate the effectiveness and generalization of our method on four datasets (both simulated and real data), showing the superiority of our method. The project page is available at https://github.com/yunfanLu/HR-INR .

title: Efficient Test-Time Prompt Tuning for Vision-Language Models
SLCA++: Unleash the Power of Sequential Fine-Tuning for Continual Learning with Pre-training
DreamMix: Decoupling Object Attributes for Enhanced Editability in Customized Image Inpainting
CLIDD: Cross-Layer Independent Deformable Description for Efficient and Discriminative Local Feature Representation
Blurring Modal Boundaries: A Unified Survey from Single- to Multi-modal Person Re-ldentification
Semantic Privacy Protection with Utility Preservation for 3D Point Clouds
abstract: Abstract Point cloud data face serious semantic privacy risks during acquisition, transmission, and cross-institutional sharing. Existing methods mostly rely on geometric perturbation or destructive encryption, which can reduce the recognizability of the original class but often impair downstream usability. This paper proposes a class-transfer-based semantic encryption framework for point clouds, aiming to conceal original class information while preserving task utility and supporting authorized recovery. Specifically, we construct a unified latent space with a shared-backbone Normalizing Flow, and combine LoRA and FiLM to achieve parameter-efficient class-conditional adaptation. We further introduce diffusion-guided flow alignment to regularize the latent distribution, construct an energy-based category transition graph, and obtain an optimal class-transfer table through global matching. Then, a latent-space Neural ODE continuously evolves source-class latents into target-class latents, which are decoded into target-class point clouds through the inverse flow. We adopt attacker-oriented metrics, including New-Class Recognition Rate (NCRR), Original-Class Leakage Rate (OCLR), and Original Label Recovery Rate (OLRR), to evaluate privacy and utility. Experiments on classification and segmentation benchmarks show that the proposed method achieves controllable semantic transformation, effectively reduces original-class semantic leakage, preserves downstream learnability in the protected domain, and supports reliable authorized reconstruction.

title: Socialality Anchors: Towards Group-Bounded Trajectory Prediction
DLCL: Deep Learning-Enabled Cooperative Localization for UAV-UGV Team with Adaptive Perception Recovery
authors: Veera Venkata Ram Murali Krishna Rao Muvva

title: MC-PanDA++: Simpler, Stronger, and More Robust Domain-Adaptive Panoptic Segmentation
Progressive Focused Transformer for Image Restoration
DOME: A Decoupled Offline-Online Memory Externalization Framework for Interpretable Domain-Generalized Face Anti-spoofing
Fix Your Downsampling ASAP! Aliasing and Sinc Artifact Free Pooling in the Fourier Domain
abstract: Abstract Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) are successful in various computer vision tasks. From an image and signal processing point of view, this success is counter-intuitive, as the inherent spatial pyramid design of most CNNs is apparently violating basic signal processing laws, i.e. the Sampling Theorem in their downsampling operations. This issue has been broadly neglected until recent work in the context of adversarial attacks and distribution shifts showed that there is a strong correlation between the vulnerability of CNNs and aliasing artifacts induced by bandlimit-violating downsampling. As a remedy, we propose an alias-free downsampling operation in the frequency domain, denoted Frequency Low Cut Pooling (FLC Pooling) which we further extend to Aliasing and Sinc Artifact-free Pooling (ASAP) . ASAP is alias-free and removes further artifacts from sinc-interpolation. Our experimental evaluation on ImageNet-1k, ImageNet-C and CIFAR datasets on various CNN architectures demonstrates that networks using FLC Pooling and ASAP as downsampling methods learn more stable features as measured by their robustness against common corruptions and adversarial attacks, while maintaining a clean accuracy similar to the respective baseline models.

title: AdaEA++: Enhanced Adaptive Model Ensemble Adversarial Attack for Boosting Adversarial Transferability
Controllable Human-Object Interaction Synthesis via Progressive and Invertible Condition Injection
RDD: Improving Structure from Motion with a Robust Feature Detector and Descriptor
abstract: Abstract Robust feature detection and description are core components of 3D vision pipelines, yet they remain challenging under large viewpoint, scale, and appearance changes. Recent methods have improved local feature learning, but many still rely on convolutional operators whose local receptive fields limit their ability to capture long-range geometric cues. We present Robust Deformable Detector (RDD), a robust keypoint detector and descriptor that uses deformable transformers to capture global context and geometric invariance. Deformable attention allows the descriptor branch to focus on a sparse set of informative locations, reducing the effective search space while preserving the ability to model long-range relationships. We also collect an Air-to-Ground dataset for training and evaluation, complementing the standard MegaDepth dataset. RDD outperforms state-of-the-art keypoint detection and description methods in sparse matching and also supports semi-dense matching. To support comprehensive evaluation, we introduce two challenging benchmarks: MegaDepth-View, which emphasizes large viewpoint and scale variations, and Air-to-Ground, which targets cross-altitude matching for 3D reconstruction. Project page: https://xtcpete.github.io/rdd/ .

title: Ultra-High-Definition Image Restoration via Prior-driven Patch Bilateral Compensation
Boundary-Aware Model with Deformable Feature Warping for Sparse-View Reconstruction
RS-vHeat+: An Efficient Remote Sensing Foundation Model Guided by Multi-Modal Fine-Grained Visual Semantics via Heat Conduction
NightFEST: A Feature-Enhanced SpatioTemporal fusion method for Nighttime light data from SDGSAT-1 GLI and NPP-VIIRS
A novel framework for urban–rural gradient classification by integrating multidimensional urbanization features via self-supervised learning
venue: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation
abstract: Rapid urbanization has transformed vast natural landscapes into increasingly complex human-dominated environments, giving rise to pronounced urban–rural gradients. However, accurate classification of such gradients remains challenging because biophysical indicators alone cannot fully represent the socioeconomic heterogeneity embedded in the urban–rural continuum. Here, based on multisource Earth observation and geospatial datasets, we propose a novel urban–rural gradient classification framework that integrates multidimensional urbanization features, including, land development, population density, economic intensity, and social vitality, to establish a five-class urban–rural gradient classification scheme-Urban core, Urban area, Suburban area, Rural area, and Natural area. Then, we developed URGCNet, a spatial clustering-driven self-supervised learning model that incorporates ordinal constraints to capture the ordered structure of the urban–rural continuum. Based on this framework, we produced URGCdataset, a 500 m urban–rural gradient classification dataset for mainland China for five benchmark years (2005, 2010, 2015, 2020, and 2025). The framework achieved strong classification performance, with URGCNet reaching an overall accuracy of 91.0% and URGCdataset reaching 93.6% against an independent test sample dataset. Ablation experiments show that removing individual urbanization features reduced the Kappa coefficient by 0.1–0.2, highlighting the indispensable role of socioeconomic information beyond biophysical indicators. Spatiotemporal analysis reveals a clear expansion of human-activity areas over the 2005–2025 period, during which the share of natural areas decreased from 92.7% to 90.0%. Overall, this framework provides a transferable pathway for establishing comparable urban–rural gradient classifications across diverse regional contexts and offers a new spatial foundation for urban environmental and ecological applications.

title: A framework for inversion and assimilation of deep-sea mirror ocean acoustic tomography observations
venue: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation
abstract: The deep ocean plays a critical role in the global climate system. However, satellite Earth observation is limited to the sea surface, while in-situ measurements struggle to achieve synchronous coverage over vast oceanic areas. Ocean Acoustic Tomography (OAT) is an essential method for retrieving large-scale interior ocean parameters; however, its path-integral nature leads to high-dimensional and ill-posed inverse problems when applied to the deep ocean. To address this, this paper develops a unified modular framework for the inversion and assimilation of acoustic remote sensing data, specifically designed for Mirror OAT (MOAT) in the deep sea. Through a configurable dimensionality reduction representation, the framework regularizes the ill-posed inverse problem in a low-dimensional space, enabling a stable and efficient numerical solution. High-resolution ocean model-based simulation experiments are conducted to evaluate its performance. Results show that the inversion module reconstructs 3-D flow fields via a “section-to-plane” two-step method, with inversion errors below 0.15 m/s over most of the water column relative to the true fields from the high-resolution ocean model. The assimilation module integrates observations using an Ensemble Kalman Filter based on a low-dimensional subspace, improving the analysis field accuracy by approximately 35 % compared to the background field. Further sensitivity experiments indicate that the assimilation method exhibits superior robustness against observation noise, while the inversion method offers higher computational efficiency by requiring neither an ensemble of model forecasts nor sequential cycling. Parameter analyses provide a basis for selecting the appropriate approach under different scenarios. This study provides a complete workflow, from methodology to numerical validation, for efficient and accurate estimation of deep-sea interior states from MOAT observations. It may serve as a reference for the design and operational application of deep-sea 3-D remote sensing observation systems.

title: Image-projected apparent particle size distribution estimation in rock avalanches using direct deep regression from UAV imagery
venue: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation
abstract: Due to the rapid downslope movement of fragmented rock masses, rock avalanches are among the most destructive geomorphic hazards in mountainous regions. Particle size characteristics observed at the surface provide useful information for interpreting fragmentation, transport, and depositional patterns. Recent advances in unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV)-based remote sensing and deep learning have enabled novel methodologies for PSD estimation. However, achieving rapid acquisition and reliable PSD characterization under complex field conditions remains challenging. To address these challenges, we constructed and preprocessed a dedicated UAV dataset for PSD analysis from high-resolution RGB imagery acquired with a DJI Matrice 300 RTK platform. Based on this dataset, we proposed a direct deep regression pipeline to predict characteristic image-projected apparent PSD descriptors, including D 20 , D 40 , D 60 , D 80 , and D max , directly from UAV image patches. The proposed approach was compared with two baseline methods: handcrafted feature-based regression and semantic segmentation-based contour pipelines. Experimental results showed that the direct deep regression pipeline achieved better overall PSD prediction performance than the baseline approaches, with ConvNeXt-Tiny obtaining the lowest mean absolute error (MAE) of 2.23 cm and resolution-normalized MAE of 16.77 ground sampling distance (GSD) units. The model exhibited more stable predictive performance for the intermediate percentiles (D 40 –D 80 ), whereas relatively higher errors were observed for D 20 and D max . The trained model was applied to representative areas within the study deposit to generate spatial maps of surface-visible apparent PSD, demonstrating its potential for UAV-based characterization of surface particle size patterns in fragmented rock deposits. Additional transfer validation on tunnel boring machine (TBM)-excavated rock images provides preliminary evidence of cross-scenario transferability across different material and imaging conditions. True cross-event validation on independent rock avalanche deposits remains to be conducted.

title: Integrated remote sensing and geotechnical investigations of the 2022 Jiujiawan mudstone landslide in Xining city, China: from deformation monitoring to failure mechanisms
venue: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation
abstract: Mudstone landslides are widespread worldwide, with their initiation and evolution mainly governed by the coupled effects of rock mass microstructure and hydromechanical behavior. However, the linkage between Earth observation (EO)-derived deformation signals and microscale weakening mechanisms remains poorly constrained. Using the catastrophic Jiujiawan landslide (15 September 2022, Xining, China) as a case study, this research aims to reconstruct the spatiotemporal evolution of the landslide and explain the multiscale mechanisms connecting microscale material degradation with macroscale slope failure through evidence-based interpretation. To achieve this, an integrated framework combining multisource EO data, geotechnical investigations, and laboratory analyses was applied. This approach clarifies deformation characteristics and failure mechanisms from coupled macro- and microscale perspectives. At the macroscopic scale, a high-fidelity three-dimensional model was reconstructed using unmanned aerial vehicle photogrammetry. Satellite optical imagery was used to qualitatively trace the pre-failure evolutionary trajectory, complemented by interferometric synthetic aperture radar to quantitatively reconstruct spatiotemporal displacement sequences. At the microscopic scale, X-ray diffraction, scanning electron microscopy, and energy dispersive spectroscopy characterized the mineralogical suite and microstructural fabric. These analyses reveal the properties of Paleogene mudstone intercalated with gypsum layers, showing how pore-fracture networks accelerate rock mass degradation. Synthesis of the results indicates a process-based linkage whereby microscale hydromechanical weakening (clay mineral hydration, argillization, and gypsum dissolution) is progressively manifested as macroscopic creep and acceleration in EO-derived displacement time series, with seismic preconditioning (the 2022 Ms 6.9 Menyuan earthquake) further reducing the slope’s structural threshold through mechanical fatigue, ultimately leading to slope failure under extreme precipitation. This transferable multiscale framework supports mechanism-informed hazard assessment and enables EO‑based early detection and staged early warning for clay‑rich, water‑sensitive slopes that undergo progressive creep under hydromechanical coupling, especially during extreme climatic events.

title: A method for identifying urban flood inundation based on single-temporal remote sensing imagery
abstract: Rapid mapping of urban flood inundation is critical for emergency response and decision-making. However, existing methods often rely heavily on multi-temporal data or deep learning models, limiting their timeliness and computational efficiency. This study proposes an automated method for mapping urban flood inundation from a single post-event image acquired by the Sentinel-2 Multispectral Instrument. The method adopts a three-stage framework comprising spectral-index-based segmentation, morphological-feature-based separation, and spatial-topological assessment. It was evaluated using three flood events in Zhengzhou, China; Manville, United States; and Porto Alegre, Brazil. Independent validation yielded overall accuracies of 0.9985, 0.9371, and 0.8834; precision values of 0.6719, 0.6771, and 0.8229; and F1-scores of 0.8037, 0.7001, and 0.7615, respectively. The extracted flood extents were further compared with those obtained using two conventional approaches and were generally consistent across the three study areas. Agreement F1-scores ranged from 0.694 to 0.870 relative to pre- and post-flood change detection based on the modified normalised difference water index, and from 0.603 to 0.866 relative to newly inundated area extraction using the European Commission Joint Research Centre permanent surface-water mask. On an experimental platform equipped with an NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin, processing the Porto Alegre, Manville, and Zhengzhou scenes required 24.3, 2.68, and 19.8 s, respectively. These quantitative results indicate that the proposed method can identify major urban flood inundation areas under diverse geographical and hydrological conditions. Requiring only a single post-event multispectral image, no model training, and no high-performance computing, the method provides a lightweight solution for rapid urban flood inundation mapping and resource-constrained applications, including onboard satellite processing.

title: UniColorFlow: A Unified Framework for Multimodal-Guided Video Colorization with Consistency Flow
Unveiling Representation Expansion: A New Lens on Out-of-Distribution Detection
An improved GNSS-R ocean scatterometry recalibration approach using gradient boosting decision tree
abstract: Spaceborne Global Navigation Satellite System Reflectometry (GNSS-R) has developed rapidly for ocean scatterometry over the past three decades. However, residual signal calibration errors, arising from inaccuracies in some key parameters and the complex space environment, degrade its performance. In this work, we propose a one-step signal recalibration framework based on Gradient Boosting Decision Tree (GBDT) in a scaling correction manner guided by qualitative analyses. Results show good alignment between the learned and theoretical correction factors, wherein the bin ratio (BR) exhibits the dominant contribution. The recalibrated σ 0 exhibits lower sensitivity to calibration-related input features than the Cyclone Global Navigation Satellite System (CYGNSS) Version 2.1 (V2.1) σ 0 , and for several parameters, also lower sensitivity than the Version 3.2 (V3.2) σ 0 produced using traditional step-wise corrections during the period from January to June 2019. The maximum deviation of σ 0 across different wind speeds is also substantially reduced, leading to root mean square error (RMSE) of 1.52 m/s for ocean wind speed retrievals over 0–27 m/s, an improvement of 17.4% and 16.0% compared to using the V2.1 and V3.2 σ 0 products, respectively. Validation against buoy wind speed data shows an RMSE of 1.29 m/s and a bias of 0.020 m/s, representing reductions of 17.3% and 87.1%, respectively, relative to retrievals using the V3.2 σ 0 product. Feature importance analysis using SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) confirms consistency with theoretical expectations, especially regarding coupling effects between input features. The recalibrated σ 0 exhibits significantly reduced dependence on BR, GNSS-R satellites antennas, and Global Positioning System (GPS) transmitters, simultaneously. Furthermore, the spatial distribution of correction factors is strongly correlated with the noise floor, indicating that the proposed GBDT model identifies high-noise cases through BR and improves the robustness of σ 0 in these high-noise regions. As an alternative to step-wise empirical correction methods that could introduce artificial biases, the proposed recalibration method provides a new perspective and potential pathway for improving GNSS-R scatterometry.

title: Estimating hourly surface global and diffuse solar radiation across China using virtual radiation station networks
Integrating anthropogenic hydrodynamics and GOCI satellite observations for water quality retrieval in highly engineered coastal systems: A case study of Saemangeum
Detection of soil moisture variations beneath an asphalt layer using L-band SAR
venue: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation
abstract: Synthetic aperture radar (SAR)-based soil moisture retrieval has primarily focused on bare or vegetated surfaces, whereas asphalt generally considered a highly attenuating medium that limits the detection of subsurface soil. Here, we used an L-band SAR sensor in a microwave anechoic chamber to characterize the detectable depth through asphalt and its controlling factors, and further quantitatively investigate the responses of interferometric phase, coherence, and closure phase to infiltration-induced variations in subsurface soil moisture. Results show subsurface echoes remain detectable through at least 9 cm of asphalt using an L-band Mini-SAR, while modeling indicates that increasing transmit power and antenna aperture could extend detectable depth beyond 30 cm. The InSAR observables exhibited distinct responses to infiltration-induced subsurface moisture variations. The mean interferometric phase decreased linearly with increasing soil volumetric water content (VWC) ( r = - 0.992 ), with an average phase shift of approximately 0.53° per 1 % increase in VWC. Spatial analysis further revealed a strong correspondence between regions of reduced coherence and nonzero closure phase and the infiltration-affected area. Overall, this study provides theoretical and methodological support for improving the subsurface detectability of airborne and vehicle-based L-band SAR sensors and for InSAR-based detection of soil moisture variations beneath asphalt layers.

title: InterMine: A foundation model-based multi-task interaction network for remote sensing interpretation of open-pit coal mining activity
venue: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation
abstract: The interpretation of open-pit coal mining activity is critical for resource management and ecological protection. It comprises two key tasks: extent extraction and fine-grained change detection. However, existing methods usually suffer from task separation, and their outputs cannot fully meet the requirements of interpretation. Therefore, this study proposes a foundation model-based multi-task interaction network (InterMine) to jointly perform open-pit mine extent extraction and fine-grained change detection. First, InterMine employs a Siamese foundation model as the encoder to enhance feature representation from images of complex open-pit coal mines and incorporates a channel-spatial feature reconstruction module to adapt the encoded features to meet the semantic and spatial requirements of the decoder. Second, a multi-task interaction mechanism is proposed to facilitate complementary information exchange between tasks. Finally, a consistency loss function based on hard-sample reweighting is designed to mitigate inconsistencies among multi-task outputs. InterMine is trained and evaluated on a self-constructed multi-temporal open-pit coal mining activity interpretation dataset (OMSet). Experimental results demonstrate that InterMine outperforms the compared methods. In particular, InterMine achieves F1-scores of 87.57 %, 83.68 %, and 79.43 % for open-pit mine extent extraction, excavation change detection, and reclamation change detection, respectively, outperforming the comparison methods by 1.89 ∼ 5.29, 3.04 ∼ 7.83, and 2.79 ∼ 7.42 percentage points, respectively. This work provides both technical and data support for open-pit coal mine monitoring. OMSet and the code of InterMine have been made publicly available at https://figshare.com/s/03c029d8e4846faef69f .

title: Density-dominated aggregation and spatiotemporal differentiation of yellow sea green tides revealed by long term observations
venue: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation
abstract: Green tides dominated by Ulva prolifera have bloomed in the Yellow Sea since 2008, posing persistent threats to coastal ecosystems. While multiple indicators (including bloom extent, pixel area, coverage area, and biomass) have been used to characterize bloom dynamics, their inconsistent use may obscure assessments of bloom intensity and spatiotemporal variability, leaving their variations across spatial perspectives poorly understood and limiting their practical utility for green tide management. Here, we investigate how the interannual dynamics of Yellow Sea green tides during 2008–2024 differ when evaluated in terms of biomass rather than bloom extent, and the spatial patterns underlying these differences. The annual biomass variability peaked at 3.6 times the long-term average, exceeding the 2.0 times observed for bloom extent. This indicates increasingly dense and aggregated U. prolifera distributions and an underestimation of interannual bloom intensity by bloom extent. In the Subei Bank Front (SBF) perspective, MODIS observations show that U. prolifera first appear near the SBF in early May. U. prolifera biomass in the northern region closely tracked annual biomass across the Yellow Sea, making it the dominant contributor to interannual bloom variability, while the southern region accounted for only 17 %. From the nearshore perspective (within 20 km of the coastline), nearshore green tide biomass has largely remained below the 2008 level (49.90 kt) over the past 16 years, except in 2015 (53.54 kt) and 2019 (70.33 kt), which exceeded it by 7 % and 41 %. The cross-validation identified the annual biomass series excluding the 20 km coastal zone and the region north of the SBF as robust proxies for annual mean biomass under data gaps, with the former yielding a substitution error of 8 %. These findings provide critical quantitative evidence for Yellow Sea green tide monitoring and sustainable coastal ecosystem management in support of SDG 14.2.

title: Fine-scale annual mapping and dynamic monitoring of shrub encroachment in alpine grasslands by integrating Sentinel-2 phenological features with Sentinel-1 structural information
venue: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation
abstract: Shrub encroachment can alter forage resources, soil–water processes, and landscape configuration in alpine grasslands, yet annual mapping remains challenging because shrub and herbaceous canopies converge spectrally and many apparent changes occur in diffuse ecotones. We developed a 10-m annual mapping framework integrating Sentinel-2 phenology, Sentinel-1 synthetic aperture radar (SAR) time-series information, and topographic covariates to distinguish shrubland from grassland in Maqu County on the northeastern Tibetan Plateau from 2018 to 2024. A learned SAR-derived shrubland-grassland discrimination score (SGDS) was constructed from annual Sentinel-1 descriptors using least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO)-regularized logistic regression to improve shrubland-grassland discrimination. In the 2024 benchmark experiment, the selected random forest (RF) configuration reduced classification error by approximately 17% relative to optical-only RF. SGDS outperformed the tested conventional SAR indices and the full SAR-statistics feature set, and adding SGDS increased RF accuracy from 91.26% to 92.47%. When the selected workflow was applied independently to each mapping year, annual overall accuracies ranged from 91.6% to 95.8%, based on the same 500 temporally screened reference locations spatially separated from the model-development samples. Nominal mapped shrubland area increased from 392.3 km2 in 2018 to 648.2 km2 in 2022 before declining to 560.4 km2 in 2024. Confidence and boundary-sensitivity analyses showed that the pronounced 2020–2021 increase was largely associated with low-confidence ecotonal pixels and decreased from + 96.91 to + 6.09 km2 as the mapped-class confidence threshold increased from 0.60 to 0.80, whereas the 2022–2024 decline remained negative under all tested confidence and boundary screens. Mapped shrubland area showed an apparent positive association with annual mean temperature, but this relationship was not robust after detrending and should be considered preliminary given the seven-year record. Overall, integrating learned SAR structural information with optical phenology improved annual shrubland-grassland mapping and provided a more reliable basis for interpreting mapped dynamics, with potential for locally calibrated application in comparable alpine regions.

title: GUARD-net: A geostationary satellite-based network for near-real-time active fire detection under class imbalance
A spatially-adaptive automated sample generation framework via multi-source phenological fusion for large-scale crop mapping: demonstrated on peanuts in Shandong, China
venue: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation
abstract: Accurate regional-scale crop mapping is critical for agricultural monitoring but remains persistently hindered by two fundamental challenges: limited inter-class separability arising from the high spectral-temporal similarity of co-occurring crops, and a label scarcity bottleneck exacerbated by the spatial non-stationarity of crop phenology. To address these limitations, this study proposes a novel Spatially-Adaptive Automated Sample Generation (SAASG) framework. By integrating multi-source remote sensing data with an iterative transfer learning strategy, SAASG autonomously generates high-fidelity training samples across heterogeneous landscapes. The framework’s core innovations are twofold. First, we engineer a Multi-source Phenological Feature Curve (MPFC) that synergizes the orthogonal information of Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) backscatter, the optical Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI), and a newly developed Contrast-Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (CNDVI). The CNDVI employs a novel spectro-structural modulation mechanism specifically designed to resolve late-season asymptotic saturation. Second, we introduce a Spatially-Adaptive Iterative Domain Adaptation mechanism utilizing a grid-based migration strategy. This discretizes the region into local domains to iteratively propagate phenological knowledge, effectively minimizing domain shift errors through spatial ensemble constraints. Demonstrated on peanuts in Shandong Province, China, the SAASG-generated samples exhibit superior phenological fidelity (Sequence Consistency Score = 0.982 ± 0.008; DTW distance = 0.172 ± 0.050) and possess a statistical distribution statistically congruent with in-situ ground-truth data. Leveraging these automatically labeled samples, we produced a 10-m resolution provincial peanut map with robust accuracy (Overall Accuracy > 0.85) across diverse agro-ecological zones. Crucially, a controlled substitution test confirmed that the classifier trained solely on SAASG samples achieved performance comparable to one trained on labor-intensive field data (ΔOA < 3%). These results confirm that the proposed framework provides a physically interpretable and operationally scalable solution to the training data crisis, enabling reliable large-scale mapping in regions with limited ground observations.

title: A multi-scale retrieval of three-dimensional ocean temperature by merging satellite and in situ observations
venue: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation
abstract: Ocean temperature is a key variable in ocean dynamics, exerting broad impacts on the climate and ecosystems. In this study, we develop a multi-scale Bayesian hierarchical modeling framework to retrieve the three-dimensional (3D) ocean temperature by combining satellite and in situ observations. The retrieval process consists of two steps. The first step is to map the subsurface temperature anomaly ( T a ) relative to a climatological seasonal cycle based on satellite-measured sea surface temperature anomaly (SSTA) and sea surface height anomaly (SSHA). The mapping function is estimated from a geographically and seasonally varying coefficient (GSVC) linear regression model to capture the varying mapping relationship caused by the variations of ocean context with space and season. The second step is to fuse the mapped T a with in situ observations under a Bayesian hierarchical modeling framework. This allows the data fusion to take into consideration the mapping errors of T a due to not only variations of T a independent of SSTA and SSHA but also uncertainties in the estimated mapping function. The above mapping-fusion procedure is conducted separately on large-scale and mesoscale ocean processes to account for their distinct characteristics. Application of our method to the Indian Ocean sector of the Southern Ocean yields more accurate retrieval of 3D ocean temperature than a state-of-the-art data product, based on independent in situ test data.

title: FGPMamba: Frequency-geometry prior-guided Mamba for building change detection
venue: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation
abstract: Building change detection (BCD) from high-resolution optical remote sensing imagery supports urban monitoring, land-use mapping, and construction progress assessment. However, in arid emerging-city environments, bare land, construction surfaces, concrete roofs, roads, and shadows may resemble changed buildings, resulting in pseudo changes, incomplete regions, and uncertain boundaries. This study proposes a frequency-geometry prior-guided Mamba network (FGPMamba) that combines global context modeling, phase-preserving frequency-domain feature recalibration, gradient-guided global–local fusion, and absolute-difference-based gradient refinement to exploit structural and boundary cues under appearance ambiguity. We also construct the African Desert Emerging-City Building Change Detection dataset (ADEC-CD) using 2018 and 2024 SuperView-2 imagery of Egypt’s New Administrative Capital. ADEC-CD adopts a geographically independent multi-zone split to reduce spatial leakage. On its geographically held-out test set, FGPMamba achieves mean F1, I o U 1 , Kappa, B-F1, and B-IoU scores of 87.49%, 77.76%, 86.70%, 64.78%, and 40.25%, respectively, over three independent runs. Under dataset-specific training and evaluation, FGPMamba also achieves the highest F1, B-F1, and B-IoU scores among the compared methods on SYSU-CD and HRCUS-CD. Controlled comparisons and feature-response analyses show that the proposed design improves pseudo-change suppression, changed-region completeness, and boundary reliability through frequency-dependent recalibration and boundary-concentrated refinement. These results indicate the potential of FGPMamba for construction monitoring in the study area and potentially similar arid environments. The code and dataset will be publicly available at: https://github.com/zjd1836/FGPMamba .

title: G2S2-IR: Glocal Gaussian Splatting with Surface Awareness for Inverse Rendering
Geometry-aware dynamic convolutional network for instance-level segmentation of Martian landforms from high-resolution Digital Elevation Model-derived point clouds
venue: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation
abstract: Analysis and interpretation of Martian surface landforms is one of the key topics in deep-space research, offering insights into the planet’s geological evolution and history of water activity. Automated extraction of Martian landforms can greatly assist researchers in rapidly locating and analyzing regions of interest. Therefore, instance segmentation based on remote sensing data represents a promising direction for automation in planetary science. To address the challenges of indistinct landform boundaries and over-segmentation in Martian remote sensing scenes, we propose an end-to-end 3D deep learning instance segmentation framework based on dynamic convolution. In this framework, we incorporate geometric information prediction of Martian landforms to enhance the network’s perception of morphological characteristics, bluewhich improves the separation of adjacent same-class instances. During training, we introduce two feature-space constraints-“pull” and “push” forces-to reduce intra-instance variance while increasing inter-instance separability. The proposed geometry-aware dynamic convolution framework is evaluated on a self-constructed water-formed landform dataset, an impact crater dataset, and a rock dataset from Mars rover perspective and achieves AP of 41.9 ± 0.1%, 63.7 ± 0.3%, and 68.6 ± 0.2%, remaining competitive with recent transformer-based methods such as Mask3D while outperforming clustering- and dynamic-convolution-based baselines. This end-to-end framework provides valuable technical support for subsequent geomorphological interpretation and potential exploration on Mars.

title: Topology-preserving river vectorization via HydroSAM and differentiable graph optimization under coarse labels
venue: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation
abstract: Accurate river-network extraction supports global hydrological management and environmental monitoring. Automated extraction from remote-sensing imagery remains challenging because river morphology is highly variable, fine tributaries have weak visual signals, canopy and infrastructure can obscure channels, and dense annotations are scarce or spatially incomplete. Conventional raster predictions can also be fragmented and lack structural continuity. We present HydroSAM, a three-stage framework for raster extraction and topology-aware vectorization. A frozen SAM 2 Hiera encoder is adapted with QV-LoRA and the proposed Directional Curvilinear Prior Injection (DCPI), while a gated Digital Elevation Model (DEM) branch contributes coarse-scale topographic context. Segmentation is produced in a zero-prompt setting by the native SAM 2 mask decoder. A graph-guided differentiable vectorization stage then converts probability maps into connected parametric river networks. We also present M2Hydro, a benchmark containing 7,947 high-resolution 4096 × 4096 source image-annotation pairs across China. In single-run tests, HydroSAM-MM attains an F1 of 0.6995 and clDice of 0.7753 on M2Hydro. The evaluations indicate that HydroSAM supports parameter-efficient adaptation and is more resilient to the evaluated cross-regional domain shift than the convolutional and Transformer baselines.

title: Thinking on maps: how foundation model agents explore, remember, and reason in map environments
abstract: Map environments provide a fundamental medium for representing spatial structure and supporting navigation, planning, and geographic analysis. Understanding how foundation model (FM) agents acquire, consolidate, and utilize spatial knowledge in such environments is therefore critical for enabling reliable map-based reasoning and applications. However, most existing evaluations assess spatial ability in passive and non-interactive settings, without requiring models to actively explore environments, accumulate observations, and progressively construct spatial knowledge. Consequently, how spatial knowledge is formed during exploration and used for reasoning remains poorly understood. In this paper, we propose an interactive evaluation framework to examine how FM agents explore, remember, and reason in symbolic map environments. Agents incrementally navigate partially observable grid-based maps composed of roads, intersections, and points of interest (POIs), receiving only local observations at each step. Spatial understanding is then evaluated through a suite of tasks, including direction judgement, distance estimation, proximity judgement, POI density recognition, and path planning. By systematically varying exploration strategies, memory representations, and reasoning schemes across multiple foundation models, we identify distinct functional roles of these components. Exploration mainly affects experience acquisition but has a limited influence on final reasoning accuracy. In contrast, memory representation plays a central role in consolidating spatial experience, with structured memories—particularly sequential and graph-based forms—substantially improving performance on structure-intensive tasks such as path planning. Reasoning schemes further shape how stored spatial knowledge is utilized, with advanced prompting strategies supporting stronger multi-step inference. We also observe performance saturation across model versions and scales beyond a certain capability threshold, suggesting that further gains in map-based spatial understanding may depend more on spatially specialized representations and reasoning mechanisms than on model scaling alone. Overall, this work advances process-oriented evaluation of spatial cognition in FM agents and offers practical insights for building more reliable map-based reasoning systems.

title: Assessing heat dome effects on forest dynamics in the Pacific Northwest using Planet imagery
abstract: Abstract Increasingly frequent extreme heat events are imposing significant stress on forest ecosystems, with implications for forests and the organisms that live in them. This study evaluates the effects of the June 2021 Pacific Northwest (PNW) heatdome (a prolonged high-pressure system that generated record-breaking temperatures) on forest canopy health and its subsequent recovery within the conifer-dominated Ellsworth Creek Preserve in Washington state, USA, using high-resolution Planet Labs satellite imagery. We analyzed normalized difference vegetation index (NDVI) trends from spring to fall from 2017 to 2024 to identify canopy stress and quantify changes in canopy greenness. Experimental forest restoration thinning treatments implemented to test their effectiveness in restoring old-growth forest characteristics at our sites allowed us to assess impacts of the heatdome event relative to these restoration treatments. Our results show a marked decline in summer NDVI following the 2021 heatdome, signaling substantial canopy stress. This decline, different than patterns in the other seven years, was particularly strong in dense, unmanaged (control) forest stands, which exhibited more pronounced NDVI declines than thinned (treatment) stands. These more pronounced stress signals during and after the heat event were associated with greater tree canopy height, canopy complexity, and tree density. The summer NDVI trends over the three post-heatdome years suggest a gradual recovery in tree canopy greenness, with thinned stands showing faster NDVI recovery than controls. In all, these results suggest that restoration thinning may improve canopy resilience to extreme heat. However, recovery trajectories varied widely within stand types, with persistent evidence of stress in high-density areas that suggest incomplete recovery as of 2023. Broadly, these findings show the vulnerability of dense forest canopies to extreme heat events, suggesting that forests with high canopy density may be less adaptable to recurring heat events. Nonetheless, managing forests through restoration thinning may enhance forest resilience to these climate-induced stressors – providing potential guidance for adaptive management strategies to maintain forest health in a world with more extreme climates.

title: Elevation-dependent regulation of alpine vegetation productivity by snow cover and grazing on the Tibetan Plateau under a warming–wetting climate
venue: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation
abstract: Grassland productivity on the Tibetan Plateau (TP) is fundamental to regional carbon cycling and ecosystem functioning and is strongly regulated by snow dynamics and grazing under a changing climate. However, the mechanisms by which alpine grassland productivity responds to interacting climatic, cryospheric, and anthropogenic drivers remain poorly constrained. Here, we integrated long-term multi-source Earth observation data to quantify the spatiotemporal trends of grassland gross primary productivity (GPP) across the TP from 1982 to 2018 and examined the relationships between GPP and snow dynamics, climate, and grazing intensity, with an explicit emphasis on elevation-dependent controls. Our results reveal a pronounced nonlinear reorganization of GPP controls along elevation gradients, with a critical transition zone at mid-elevations (∼3500–4000 m). Within this zone, warming exerted the strongest positive association with GPP, while grazing intensity also showed a positive spatial association with GPP. In contrast, at higher elevations (>4500 m), snow dynamics emerged as dominant constraints on GPP. Structural equation modeling further indicates that snow cover duration showed the strongest negative total effect among the modeled environmental variables, whereas grazing intensity showed an elevation – dependent association with GPP, shifting from a positive spatial correlation at mid – elevations to a negative correlation at high elevations. Across all elevation zones, soil moisture-mediated pathways consistently exert stronger controls on GPP than soil temperature pathways, highlighting water availability as the more direct and dominant constraint on alpine grassland productivity. These findings demonstrate that elevation fundamentally regulates the spatial organization of ecosystem productivity controls on the TP and underscore the importance of explicitly accounting for cryosphere–biosphere–human interactions when assessing alpine carbon dynamics under a warming and wetting climate.

title: Active CO2 lidar extends satellite monitoring of urban fossil-fuel CO2 emissions to high-aerosol cities
venue: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation
abstract: Cities with high aerosol loading are critical yet underserved targets for satellite-based monitoring of urban fossil-fuel CO 2 (ffCO 2 ) emissions, because passive XCO 2 retrievals often suffer from severe data loss and aerosol-induced uncertainty under polluted conditions. Here, we evaluate whether spaceborne active CO 2 lidar can extend satellite carbon monitoring to such observationally challenging environments. We combine CO 2 observations from the DQ-1 Aerosol and Carbon Dioxide Lidar (ACDL) with Sentinel-5P/TROPOMI NO 2 retrievals to construct an active–passive framework. Near-synchronous ACDL–TROPOMI overpasses are used to derive city-specific ffCO 2 -to-NO x emission ratios, which are then applied to TROPOMI-derived daily NO x emissions to reconstruct observation-constrained ffCO 2 variability. Among the top 100 urban ffCO 2 emitters, high-AOD cities are concentrated in the Asia–Pacific region, and under polluted conditions, DQ-1 provides 201.6% and 107.8% more effective CO 2 observations than OCO-2 and OCO-3, respectively. Applications to six high-AOD cities in North China and India reveal physically interpretable seasonal variability, with monthly emission magnitudes broadly consistent with EDGAR and ODIAC inventories (r = 0.79–0.81). These results demonstrate that active CO 2 lidar, when combined with dense NO 2 observations, can provide an independent top-down constraint to support urban carbon monitoring and mitigation assessment in polluted cities where passive carbon satellites are most limited.

title: 160 Years of Etna summit craters through a photogrammetry-based time machine
venue: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation
abstract: This study presents a quantitative, multi-temporal assessment of Etna’s summit morpho-structural evolution, spanning a 160-year (1865–2024) period. We integrated historical topographic maps with modern, high-resolution remote sensing data, including Unoccupied Aerial System surveys. Dataset-specific validation and statistical error propagation yielded root mean square errors ranging from decametric values for the earliest cartographic sources to metric values for the post-2020 datasets. The resulting topographic time series was interpreted alongside geological observations and previously published geodetic analyses. This integrated reconstruction documents the transition from a predominantly monocentric summit configuration to a highly dynamic polycentric system, and reveals contrasting morpho-structural behaviours among the four summit craters. VOR is characterized by recent constructive growth, BN and NEC by recurrent infilling followed by subsidence, whereas the SEC exhibits persistent constructive growth accompanied by progressive eastward expansion. These differences are consistent with variations in crater position, structural setting, shallow feeding-system configuration, and dominant eruptive style. The long-term evolution of the summit area is also consistent with the influence of the North-East and South Rift zones, and with published geodetic observations describing the seaward deformation of Etna’s eastern flank. Overall, the reconstructed evolution highlights the interaction between volcanic construction, structural controls, and gravitational deformation in shaping a continuously changing and asymmetric summit system. The proposed geospatial workflow provides a reproducible and transferable framework for integrating heterogeneous historical and modern topographic datasets and for investigating long-term morpho-structural change at other highly active volcanoes.

title: Improving automatic glacier mapping accuracy, robustness, and reliability across the Third Pole Region
abstract: Most automatic glacier mapping methods applied in the Third Pole Region (TPR), exhibit suboptimal accuracy for debris-covered glaciers, high sensitivity to interferences, and large uncertainty in model outputs, thereby limiting their operational utility. These challenges can be mitigated by deploying advanced deep learning models and enhancing dataset representativeness across complex imaging conditions. Accordingly, we compiled three large-scale datasets used for model development, glacier-level mapping evaluation, and cross-sensor generalisation assessment, respectively. We then evaluated several state-of-the-art deep learning networks and found that the adapted TransUNet performed best. On the test dataset, the model achieves a glacier Intersection over Union (IoU) of 90% and 83% in patches featuring debris-free and debris-covered glaciers, respectively, while maintaining robust under challenging conditions. Glacier-level validation further confirms the effective detection of glacier counts and precise outlines, with both metrics improving with glacier area and the global IoUTPR > 80%. Uncertainty quantification shows high output reliability, with expected calibration errors of 0.029 and 0.009 for the test and glacier-level test datasets, respectively. Our fully automated 2024–2025 Karakoram glacier inventory, comprising 12,981 glaciers covering a total area of ~19,484 km2, exhibits high agreement with earlier inventories and reflects current glacier state. The primary contribution of this study is the development of a scalable framework that, by optimising dataset representativeness and algorithmic architectures, significantly elevates the accuracy, robustness, reliability and operational value of glacier mapping across the TPR.

title: A source–medium–receiver framework for modeling wind-driven vegetation cooling in urban landscapes
abstract: Vegetation cooling in cities is often represented as a local, isotropic effect, although atmospheric processes can redistribute cooling beyond individual vegetation patches. This simplification may overlook the nonlocal and directionally structured nature of cooling propagation. We developed a physics-guided source–medium–receiver (SMR) framework for the Greater Bay Area of China to compare multi-source isotropic connectivity with prevailing-wind-conditioned connectivity. Vegetation-source strength was represented by the VCSI, and parameters estimated from 2021 to 2023 were frozen for an independent 2024 holdout and contrasting monsoon assessments. Cooling connectivity was modeled using a spatially varying distance-decay function, controlled by the wind speed, moisture content, surface albedo, terrain, and directional constraints from prevailing winds. In 2024, isotropic connectivity showed a stronger relationship with LST (r = −0.8069) than wind-conditioned connectivity (r = −0.7780) and local VCSI (r = −0.7757), with the same general ordering across monsoon and built-up receiver assessments. The source-level decay lengths ranged from 0.504 to 0.518 km, whereas the wind-conditioned emergent multi-source persistence increased from 4.13 to 4.88 km, reflecting cumulative field behaviors. Wind-relative decomposition further showed that annual connectivity was distributed across downwind, crosswind, and upwind pathways. These findings indicate that regional vegetation cooling is primarily characterized by distance-mediated, multi-source connectivity, while prevailing-wind direction acts as a scale- and condition-dependent modifier. This shift in perspective provides a physically grounded framework for effective urban climate analysis and precision greening strategies.
